title: Breezeway Review, Pricing & Alternatives (2026)
summary: Breezeway review for 2026: published pricing, PMS integrations, where it stops short on guest messaging and voice, and the alternatives worth comparing.
body_markdown:
Breezeway is property care software for short-term rental managers: cleaning and maintenance scheduling, mobile checklists with photo proof, inventory tracking, and a guest messaging layer on top. It publishes one entry price, $19 per month for Host Essentials, and quotes the rest. It fits managers whose weak point is turnover coordination between stays, rather than those whose weak point is the guest conversation.


## What is Breezeway?


Breezeway is an operations platform built around the work that happens between stays.[Its site](https://www.breezeway.io/) claims 350,000+ properties in 90 countries, and the module list runs from task scheduling, work coordination, checklists with a mobile app, maintenance and inventory tracking through to payments, reporting, smart locks and guest verification. A second group sits on the guest side: Messaging, Concierge, Guide for digital welcome books, Assist for 24/7 guest support, and Upsells.


The centre of gravity is the field team rather than the inbox. A cleaner opens the mobile app, works a checklist, photographs the finished room, and the property flips to ready. Everything else on the platform is arranged around that loop, which suits managers who run their own cleaning and maintenance crews rather than outsourcing them.


## How much does Breezeway cost?


Breezeway publishes one number and quotes the rest.[Its pricing page](https://www.breezeway.io/pricing) lists Host Essentials at "Starts at $19 / month" and says pricing is "based per property, billed monthly, with volume discounts for those with 5+ properties". There is a free Freemium tier. Essential Ops, Operations Pro, Ops + Guest Experience Suite, and Operations + Guest Experience are all "Get quote", as are the Concierge and Smart Locks add-ons.


For a 40-property manager that makes the real number unknowable before a sales call, which matters when you are comparing against platforms that publish a rate card. The $19 figure is a floor on the smallest plan, not a portfolio price.


## What is Breezeway good at?


Breezeway is strongest at making physical work verifiable. Checklists with photo capture turn "the unit is clean" into evidence an owner or a reviewer can look at, and the scheduling tools handle the part of turnover that falls over in practice: a same-day checkout and check-in, a cleaner who cancels, a maintenance task that has to slot between two stays.


Its integration list is the other genuine strength. The site names Hostify, TRACK, Mews, Guesty, Airbnb, Hostfully, Cloudbeds, Hostaway, Avantio, OwnerRez, Streamline, Escapia and Barefoot, which covers most of what a mid-size North American or European manager is likely to be running. For an operations tool, reading reservations reliably from the PMS is most of the job.


## Where does Breezeway fall short?


Breezeway's guest-facing half is thinner than its operations half. The platform offers automated guest messaging, which means scheduled text sent at a planned moment in the stay. That is a different capability from an agent that reads an incoming question, works out what the guest is asking, and completes the task behind it.


Phone is the clearer gap. Nothing on the site describes an AI voice agent answering the property's line, so after-hours calls still land with a person. For a manager whose 2am problem is a lockbox call rather than an unphotographed checklist, that is the wrong half of the product.


The last watch-out is the quote wall. Four of six plans carry no published price, so budgeting means a sales cycle.


## Which tools do people compare Breezeway with?


Three products overlap with Breezeway often enough to be worth scoring against it, and none of them is a substitute for the others: Operto on staff scheduling and devices, Hostaway as a system of record, and Conduit on the guest conversation. [Operto](https://operto.com/pricing/) splits into Operto ONE, Teams, Access and Guest, and leans on keyless entry and device control. Operto Teams overlaps Breezeway on staff scheduling, so managers who already run Operto locks often look there first rather than adding a second vendor.


[Hostaway](https://www.hostaway.com/features/communication/) is a PMS, so comparing it to Breezeway is a category error most of the time. It says more than 10,000 property managers use it and offers AI Replies across a unified inbox. If you are choosing a system of record it belongs on the list; if you already run one, it does not.


## Who should pick something else?


Pick something else when your bottleneck is the guest conversation rather than the turnover. Breezeway is built to coordinate people doing physical work, and it does that well. If the recurring failure in your week is an unanswered 2am call, an inbox nobody got to, or the same twenty questions asked across four channels, an operations platform will not move it.


That is the case Conduit is built for. Conduit runs voice and messaging on one agent with PMS write-back, so the agent can look up a live reservation, send a door code, or move a check-in rather than take a message. Published pricing starts at $18 per unit per month for Messaging, $30 for Guest, $36 for Guest + Devices and $48 for Full Suite, with a flat $899 per month Startup plan for portfolios up to 25 units. Across 300+ hospitality brands it handles 70 to 90% of guest conversations without a person, in 140+ languages.


Plenty of managers run both. Breezeway coordinates the cleaner, Conduit answers the guest, and the two touch at the moment a property flips to ready. If you have to choose one first, choose the one matching the complaint you hear most.


## FAQ


The answers below come from Breezeway's own published pages, read on 2026-10-05, and say so plainly wherever a figure is not published rather than estimating it. How long a vendor takes to tell you a price is itself worth knowing when you are planning a purchase.


### How much does Breezeway cost?


Breezeway publishes one price, Host Essentials starting at $19 per month, and quotes every other plan. Pricing is per property and billed monthly, with volume discounts stated for portfolios of 5+ properties, and there is a free Freemium tier.


### Does Breezeway answer guest phone calls?


Breezeway does not describe an AI voice agent answering a property's phone line anywhere on its site. It offers automated guest messaging and a 24/7 guest support product called Assist, both of which are text-based, so inbound calls still reach a person.


### Which PMSs does Breezeway integrate with?


Breezeway names Hostify, TRACK, Mews, Guesty, Airbnb, Hostfully, Cloudbeds, Hostaway, Avantio, OwnerRez, Streamline, Escapia and Barefoot on its site. That covers most mid-size short-term rental stacks, which is the main reason it slots into an existing system of record without a migration.


### Is Breezeway a PMS?


Breezeway is not a property management system. It sits alongside one and reads reservations from it, which is why its integration list matters more than it would for an all-in-one platform. Managers run it next to Guesty, Hostaway, OwnerRez or Mews rather than instead of them.


### What is the difference between Breezeway and Turno?


Breezeway covers turnover, maintenance, inventory and guest messaging across the module list on its own site. We could not load Turno's pricing page to verify its current scope or rates for this comparison, so check those directly rather than assuming the two products overlap.


### Does Breezeway work for villa and luxury rentals?


Breezeway suits villa managers who coordinate on-property staff, because checklists with photo proof handle the standards work those properties are sold on. The gap is the concierge conversation, which villa guests expect to be answered at any hour and in their own language.


### Can Breezeway replace a guest communication platform?


Breezeway can cover scheduled guest messages but not an agent that resolves inbound questions end to end. Automated messaging sends planned text at planned moments; resolving a question means reading it, deciding what is being asked, and completing the task in the PMS behind it.
